scope: The museum's reconstruction from the old accounts. No drawing, part or measurement of the lion survives. The walk, the stop and the chest full of lilies are in the texts. The size, the wood and paint, the spring, the wheels, the cranks, the gait and the latch are modern choices.
gaps: No drawing of the lion survives. Two sheets are linked to it by modern writers, both weakly.
Size, material, outer finish and weight are not documented.
The drive, the power store, the gait, the leg joints and the opening trigger are not documented. Lomazzo 1590 says only that lions went by force of wheels.
Whether a person worked it, from inside or outside, is not known.
The accounts disagree on place, date and king. They name Milan, Lyon and a hall before Francis I. A letter of 1517 from Argentan tells of a lion in its street but does not name Leonardo.
Whether this was one lion or several, and what became of any, is not known.
Whether the lilies were carved, gilt, cloth, paper or real flowers is not known.

scale_m.note: Life size by choice: no source gives a size. At rest it is 2.16 m long and 1.26 m high. The envelope also holds the 1.2 m walk and the key.

frame.origin: On the floor between the paws, where the lion stands before it walks; +X is the lion's left.
frame.transforms: Every part's position_m is the centre of its envelope box in the lion's rest frame, not relative to its parent; parents name the moving hierarchy. The carved parts are distance functions baked at load; the works are built from their own numbers.

phases.name: Six steps
phases.interpolation: ratchet, slowest as the pairs change over

phases.name: The count wheel trips, the train is caught

motion.final_hold: It holds with the chest open and the lilies forward. Nothing rewinds or resets; only the visitor starts it again.
motion.visitor_12s: The key winds, the wheels take up, six stiff steps over 1.2 m, the count wheel trips and it stops mid-stride; the chest opens after.

drive.type: spring barrel, wound by a key

input_rate.unit: turns per second at the crank shafts
input_rate.note: Two steps every 2.2 s; the spring, its store and the rate are modern choices.

drive.justification: Lomazzo 1590 writes that lions went by force of wheels. The spring barrel, the train, the cranks and the rate are the museum's reading, chosen so that wheels visibly drive stepping legs.
drive.source: Lomazzo, Idea del tempio 1590: lions went by force of wheels; the train itself is the museum's

label_en: Reconstructed from old accounts: it walks, stops and opens its chest full of lilies.
label_de: Nach alten Berichten rekonstruiert: er geht, hält an und öffnet die Brust voller Lilien.
animation_notes: One finite run of 20 s that holds at its end. No hidden reset; only the visitor starts it again.
Head, jaw and tail never move.
Legs carry the body; nothing rolls. A planted paw never slides.
The count wheel turns half a turn over the walk; the detent drops into its deep notch at the end and the train stops.
The section view takes the near flank panel off; the geometry is unchanged.

physics.verdict_en: Nothing about its mass, spring or speed is documented. The museum's numbers only make the walk readable.
physics.verdict_de: Masse, Feder und Tempo sind nicht überliefert. Die Zahlen des Museums machen den Gang nur lesbar.
